passage: After lunch in the classroom, Tushar sat on the small chair beside the teacher with his fists clenched. Ganga had been calling him a baby all morning, and when she did it again, he hit her on the arm. Now everyone was staring. "I didn't know what else to do," he said in a tight voice. The teacher waited a moment. "Hitting hurt Ganga, and it's not okay. But I'm listening. What made you so upset?" Tushar said quietly, "She kept saying it." "Next time, shout 'Stop!' loudly and come to me," said the teacher.

qa.q: What did Tushar do to Ganga?
qa.a: Tushar hit Ganga on the arm.

qa.q: Why did Tushar hit Ganga, and what was he feeling?
qa.a: Tushar felt helpless and upset because Ganga kept calling him a baby. Hitting felt like the only answer, as he said, "I didn't know what else to do."

qa.q: What could Tushar try next time, and what did the teacher do right?
qa.a: He can shout "Stop!" loudly and go to the teacher. The teacher was right to say hitting is not okay and also ask what made him so upset.

qa.q: How might Ganga have felt when Tushar hit her?
qa.a: Ganga was probably hurt and surprised. She may not have realised her teasing was getting to Tushar so much, but the hit was still not okay.

grounding: A child hits a teaser and is in trouble, feeling helpless, and the teacher says hitting is not okay, suggests saying stop loudly and asks what made him so upset.
